parsedVerdict.reasoning: The seven files serve one concern: order placement and fulfilment, plus the stock levels it depends on. Every use case reaches persistence only through the domain ports it is given (OrderRepository, ProductRepository). No file uses a database, ORM or query client directly. Converting an Order to an OrderDto always goes through the shared toOrderDto in order-mapper.ts. State rules stay on the domain objects: use cases call order.advanceTo, order.cancel and stock.reserve/release rather than repeating that logic. Status validation reads the single domain definition in order-status. AdvanceOrderUseCase calls isOrderStatus and throws its own VALIDATION error, while ListOrdersUseCase calls assertOrderStatus. That is a small inconsistency in how the failure is reported, not a copied rule, and the domain source is not shown to confirm the two errors differ. The repeated NOT_FOUND guard in two use cases is a one-line check, not a copied business rule.
